alalal-e76347-d1e101.summary: Rubric marking the division of Lombard's text for Distinction 23 of Book III.

alalal-e76347-d1e108.summary: Locates the beginning of the part of Book III on the restoring principles formally ordered to action, rather than against the defect of sin, as announced at the start of the book.

alalal-e76347-d1e127.summary: Divides this part in two: first the gracing and restoring habits, then the precepts regarding works, which begin at Distinction 37 with the distribution of the Decalogue.

alalal-e76347-d1e150.summary: Divides the treatment of habits: first knowledge of each habit singly, then their connection, from Distinction 36.

alalal-e76347-d1e174.summary: Divides the treatment of habits singly into virtues and then gifts, from Distinction 34 on the seven gifts.

alalal-e76347-d1e192.summary: Divides the virtues into theological and then cardinal, from Distinction 33 on the four virtues.

alalal-e76347-d1e215.summary: Divides the theological virtues into faith, hope (from Distinction 26) and charity (from Distinction 27).

alalal-e76347-d1e240.summary: Divides the treatise on faith into three distinctions: Distinction 23 explains two definitions of faith; Distinction 24 raises and solves doubts about this explanation, beginning 'if faith is only of things unseen'; Distinction 25 treats faith according to the state of the believer.

alalal-e76347-d1e272.summary: Divides the present distinction into three parts: Lombard first connects with what precedes, then presents Augustine's definition of faith ('Fides est virtus').

alalal-e76347-d1e288.summary: The third part presents another definition with its explanation, Hebrews 11:1, 'faith is the substance of things hoped for'.

alalal-e76347-d1e301.summary: In the second part Lombard first gives the definition of faith in its second chapter and then its explanation in the five following chapters, beginning 'Accipitur autem fides'.

alalal-e76347.summary: Division of Lombard's text locating Distinction 23 in the structure of Book III. After Christology, Lombard treats the habits that restore human action and then the precepts. The habits are virtues and gifts, the virtues are theological and cardinal, and the theological virtues are faith, hope and charity. The treatise on faith runs through Distinctions 23 to 25: the definitions of faith, doubts about them, and faith according to the believer's state. Distinction 23 itself has three parts: a transition, Augustine's definition of faith with five chapters of explanation, and the definition in Hebrews 11:1 with its explanation.
